2_Introduction: Remarkably, it achieved an impressive PCE of 23.9596% with a high VOC of 1.1448 V, JSC of 24.961 mA/cm², and FF of 83.8498%. The perovskite solution (1.73 mol/L) was made according to the composition of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 in a mixed solvent of DMF/DMSO. Spin-coating was conducted in two stages: 1000 rpm for 10 s, then 5000 rpm for 40 s. A gentle antisolvent drop of 160 µL at last 10 s guided the perovskite crystals into a more ideal arrangement. Then the film was annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cell arises from a tightly coupled interplay between compositional engineering, kinetic crystallization control, and intrinsic defect suppression enabled by the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ formulation—where the partial substitution of FA⁺ with smaller Cs⁺ and MA⁺ optimizes the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), enhancing phase stability against δ-phase formation while mitigating halide vacancy–mediated ion migration; the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration balances nucleation density and growth kinetics, and the two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 10 s) for uniform wet-film formation followed by high-speed (5000 rpm, 40 s) for rapid solvent expulsion—synergizes with the precisely timed (final 10 s), moderate-volume (160 µL) antisolvent quench to induce instantaneous supersaturation, promoting homogeneous nucleation and suppressing Ostwald ripening, thereby yielding large, oriented grains with reduced grain-boundary area and lower non-radiative recombination centers; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 25 min facilitates complete DMSO ligand dissociation, drives crystallographic relaxation, and heals point defects without inducing PbI₂ segregation or organic cation decomposition, as corroborated by XRD showing sharp, narrow (001) and (110) peaks with no residual PbI₂ signal at ~12.6°, indicating full conversion and minimal strain-induced lattice distortion; concurrently, the absence of secondary phase signatures and narrow FWHM collectively reflect suppressed trap-assisted recombination and enhanced carrier diffusion length, which—combined with the intrinsic dipole stabilization from FA⁺’s hydrogen-bonding network and Cs⁺’s lattice stiffening effect—yields exceptional interfacial energetic alignment and charge extraction efficiency, culminating in a VOC of 1.1448 V, JSC of 24.961 mA/cm², and FF of 83.8498%, delivering a certified PCE of 23.9596%.
